articles.titre: What are the main events for today?
articles.resume: EUROPEAN SESSION In the European session, we get the final French and Spanish CPI readings, as well as the second estimate of the Eurozone Q3 GDP. The final data is almost never market-moving because markets react more to preliminary figures. The same goes for the second estimate of the GDP. Therefore, the data won't change anything for the ECB, so the market reaction will likely be muted. The focus will remain on the Fed and especially US-Iran developments, as the risk-off sentiment strengthened yesterday after Trump stated that the US doesn't need a deal with Iran. articles.titre: Japan’s Katayama warns of one-sided yen moves near 160, will coordinate with US Treasury
articles.resume: Katayama’s comments make intervention a more serious risk for anyone pushing dollar-yen above 160, especially as the US has now been confirmed as a willing partner. Expect choppy, headline-driven trading around that level, with dealers alert to any reports of rate checks. The underlying pressure on the yen remains, though, as rising Fed hike expectations keep rate differentials in the dollar’s favour. The focus on fuel prices among survey respondents links New Zealand’s factory sector to the oil shock. That keeps input costs and inflation pressure in view, even as demand holds up. Election uncertainty is a near-term drag on business confidence that could weigh on investment decisions until a coalition is formed. articles.resume: Iran’s state IRNA news agency reports: “Official sources have confirmed that Sirik in Hormozgan Province has been targeted minutes ago by the enemy”. Importantly, the confirmation suggests that state media might be looking to highlight the attack, perhaps in preparation for returning to war. That fits with a recent video highlighting a rebuilt (or hidden) underground missile city. . articles.titre: US 30-year bond auction tails as demand disappoints for second straight day
articles.resume: High yield 5.441% vs 5.437% WI Tail of 0.4 basis points Bid-to-cover 2.36x vs 2.44x average Dealers awarded 11.39% vs 9.49% average The US Treasury sold $25 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday in a disappointing auction that adds to signs of softening demand at the long end of the curve. The auction stopped at 5.441%, a 0.4 basis point tail compared to the 5.437% when-issued yield. That's a deterioration from last month's 0.1 basis point tail and compares unfavourably with the six-auction average of a 0.1 basis point stop-through. For background, the National Association of Realtors publishes its existing home sales report monthly at 10 am ET, usually in the third or fourth week of the following month. articles.titre: US weekly initial jobless claims 200K vs 195K expected
articles.resume: Prior was 189K Four week average vs 194.75K prior Continuing claims vs 1710K expected The US Department of Labor publishes its weekly unemployment insurance claims report every Thursday at 8:30 am ET, or Wednesday when a holiday falls later in the week. It’s the most timely official read on the US labor market, covering the week that ended just five days earlier. The headline figure is initial jobless claims, the number of people filing for unemployment benefits for the first time. It’s a direct gauge of layoffs.
